B the B DOWNTOWN에서 나만의 행복 레시피(Find Your Own Happiness Recipe)를 발견해 보세요.

sumry: A nighttime music fountain over Jungnangcheon Stream, staged with lasers from a former Gyeongchun Line railway bridge
post_desc:
Gyeongchun Railway Bridge is an attraction in Nowon-gu that has transformed the old Gyeongchun Line railway bridge crossing the Jungnangcheon Stream into a pedestrian bridge. During the day, it serves as a walking trail offering a panoramic view of the Jungnangcheon waterway and the cityscape, but when the sun sets, it shows a completely different face as the musical fountain lights up beneath the bridge.


The Gyeongchun Railway Bridge Musical Fountain consists of a twister fountain, where water shoots up in a spiral, and a big arch fountain that draws a large arch of water. Added to this are the first four-laser and mirror technologies applied in Korea, allowing colorful beams of light to flow along the water streams and cut through the night sky of Jungnangcheon. The approximately 20-minute performance, where water and light move together to the melodies of 21 songs played through a high-quality sound system, leads to a scene that brings back memories of the old Gyeongchun Line trains.


The performance is held once a day, four days a week, from Thursday to Sunday. It starts at 8:30 PM from May to August, at 8:00 PM in September, and at 7:00 PM in October. Operations may be suspended depending on weather conditions such as rain or strong winds, so it is recommended to check before visiting. If you walk along the trail on the railway bridge and grab a spot in time for the fountain show, you can experience the coolest summer night in northeastern Seoul.

Additionally, anyone can easily and enjoyably appreciate the artworks by reading the children's commentary, which was designed based on the artwork explanatory notes by the Korean Modern and Contemporary Art Research Institute. post_desc:
Located in Seongbuk-gu, Seoul, Heungcheonsa is the very first prayer temple of the Joseon royal family. Founded in 1397 (the 6th year of King Taejo) as a prayer temple for Queen Sindeok of the Kang clan, it is also the prayer temple of Jeongneung, a designated UNESCO World Heritage site. Heungcheonsa preserves a total of 21 cultural heritages, including 3 National Designated Cultural Heritages (Treasures). With magnificent cultural assets such as the Geuknakbojeon Hall, Myeongbujeon Hall, and Daebang, along with its serene and beautiful temple scenery, it draws many citizens and tourists from both home and abroad.

sumry: A serene stone wall path stretches along the west wall of Jongmyo Shrine
post_desc: The Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path is a tranquil walkway that stretches along the western wall of Jongmyo Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Unlike well-known historical and cultural spots like Bukchon and Insadong, this pathway is a hidden gem that has recently gained popularity. Strolling along the pristine, elegant stone wall, visitors can leisurely explore nearby cafes, craft studios, and shops and cafes housed in renovated hanok buildings along the side alleys. The path is beautifully framed by the historic stone wall and lush trees, offering scenic views throughout the seasons. In spring, cherry blossoms and fresh leaves embrace the wall, creating a bright and cheerful atmosphere. In autumn, the wall is transformed into a picturesque setting draped in warm hues, perfect for a romantic walk. This peaceful spot offers an ideal escape from the busy pace of everyday life. Traditional architecture and nature are in harmonious balance, providing a calming ambiance. Jongmyo Stone Wall Path is a fantastic photo spot for capturing traces of Korea’s traditional culture. Walking along the path, visitors can conveniently explore nearby attractions, such as Changgyeonggung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace, Insadong, and Samcheong-dong, where tradition meets modernity, allowing for a well-rounded cultural experience.

sumry: A pavilion located to the west of Geoncheonggung in Gyeongbokgung Palace, used as King Gojong's study
post_desc: This building is located to the west of Geoncheonggung in Gyeongbokgung Palace. It housed about 40,000 books on Western artifacts purchased from the Qing Dynasty and was mainly used as King Gojong’s private library. Additionally, it served as a venue for enshrining portraits of kings or receiving foreign envoys. Originally constructed as a secondary building of Hamnyeongjeon Hall in Changdeokgung, it was relocated to Gyeongbokgung in 1891. The building was opened to the public in 2006, and the books previously housed there are now kept at Seoul National University's Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies and the Jangseogak Archives of the Academy of Korean Studies. In 2016, Jibokjae was transformed into a library and opened to the public. It is open from April to October, except for July and August, making it a great place to visit if you're in Gyeongbokgung during this period.

sumry: A garden of a Joseon Dynasty located inside Changdeokgung Palace
post_desc: The Secret Garden (Huwon) at Changdeokgung Palace, once used for royal entertainment and ceremonies, is a significant heritage site showcasing traditional landscaping. Covering around 446,943 square meters, this expansive royal garden still has restricted areas that remain inaccessible to the public. Historically, it was off-limits to commoners, reserved only for the Joseon royal family. Nestled against Maebong Peak of Bugaksan Mountain, the garden features several ponds, including Buyongji, home to Buyongjeong Pavilion, Aeryeonji, Jangbangji, and Banwolji. The arrangement of pavilions and buildings reflects traditional Korean architecture, demonstrating a masterful harmony between structures and nature.

sumry: A temple located on the eastern foothills of Samgaksan (Bukhansan) in Jeongneung-dong, Seongbuk-gu
post_desc: Gyeongguksa Temple, nestled on the eastern slopes of Samgaksan (now known as Bukhansan), is a historic temple founded in the late Goryeo period. Renowned for its scenic mountain surroundings and fresh spring water, it attracts many visitors. The temple complex has 17 buildings, including Geungnakbojeon (Hall of Supreme Bliss), Yeongsanjeon, Myeongbujeon, Gwaneumjeon, and Sibangseonwon. Geungnakbojeon houses the Amitabha Buddha triad, along with wooden Buddhist paintings (designated as Treasure No. 748), Shinjungtaenghwa, and Palsangtaenghwa. Sibangseonwon offers a weekly Sunday meditation session, and the temple also hosts temple stay programs at Hwanheodang and Manwoldang. As one of Seoul's significant temples, Gyeongguksa was frequently visited by former President Syngman Rhee. During his tenure as Vice President, Richard Nixon of the United States visited the temple and later described it as one of his most memorable experiences in his memoirs, even including a photograph of his visit.

post_desc: チョンミョ(宗廟)トルダムギル(石垣道)は、世界文化遺産に指定されたチョンミョ(宗廟)の西側の塀に沿って長く続く、静かで風情ある石垣道です。よく知られた歴史文化スポットであるプクチョン(北村)やインサドン(仁寺洞)とは異なり、近年新たに注目を集めているスポットです。整然とした石垣沿いをゆっくり散策しながら、周囲に並ぶカフェや工芸アトリエを楽しむのにぴったりで、路地には韓屋を改装したショップやカフェも点在しています。趣ある石垣と豊かな木々が調和し、四季折々の美しい景観が魅力です。特に春には桜と新芽が石垣を包み込み、華やかな雰囲気を醸し出し、秋には紅葉に染まる石垣道が絵のように広がり、ロマンチックな散歩に最適です。ここは、日常の喧騒を離れ、伝統建築と自然が織り成す美しい空間で心が安らぐ場所です。また、チョンミョ(宗廟)トルダムギル(石垣道)は、韓国の伝統文化を感じつつ写真撮影を楽しむフォトスポットとしてもおすすめです。さらに道を進むと、近隣のチャンギョングン(昌慶宮)やチャンドッグン(昌徳宮)、インサドン(仁寺洞)やサムチョンドン(三清洞)といった、伝統と現代が融合した名所も多く、さまざまな文化体験が楽しめます。

post_desc: 宗庙石墙路是一条静谧的石板小径，它沿着被列为世界文化遗产的宗庙西侧围墙蜿蜒伸展。与历史悠久、广为人知的名胜如北村和仁寺洞不同，这是一条新近崭露头角的胡同。漫步在这条整洁而庄重的石墙路上，您可以悠然欣赏周边的咖啡厅和手工艺工作室等，它是一条理想的散步路线，沿途可见由传统韩屋改造而成的特色商店与咖啡厅。古朴的石墙与葱郁的树木相映成趣，四季变换中展现出不同的美丽景致。春天，樱花绽放与新芽吐绿点缀着石墙，营造出绚烂多彩的氛围；秋天，枫叶将石墙路染得如火如荼，宛如一幅绚丽的画卷，非常适合浪漫的漫步。这里是一个远离喧嚣、享受悠闲散步的好去处，传统建筑之美与自然景观的和谐共生，让人心旷神怡。宗庙石墙路不仅能让您感受到韩国传统文化的韵味，也是摄影的绝佳地点。此外，沿着这条街道漫步，您还可以探访附近的昌庆宫、昌德宫、仁寺洞以及三清洞等名胜，这些地方巧妙融合了传统与现代元素，让您享受丰富多彩的文化体验。

sumry: A mountain lodge restaurant beside the Uidong valley in Bukhansan, serving neungi mushroom baeksuk and braised short ribs
post_desc:
Sogwigol Baekun Sanjang is a Korean restaurant situated by the Ui-dong Valley on the way up to Baegundae Peak in Bukhansan Mountain. As you head up to the end of Samyang-ro, the sound of the valley water greets guests first, leading to seating areas on wooden benches (pyeongsang) under the shade of trees and indoor tables.


The signature menus are Neungi Duck Baeksuk and Neungi Chicken Baeksuk, boiled for a long time with Neungi mushrooms. The broth is clear and rich, and the meat is cooked so tenderly that it pulls apart with chopsticks. If you are looking for a spicy broth, the Spicy Native Chicken Stew (Dakdoritang) is a good choice, and if you want a hearty meal, the Braised Giant Beef Short Ribs (So Wang Galbijjim) is a great option. The mildly-flavored Roasted Duck is served with lettuce wraps, and the Mushroom Hot Pot is perfect for sharing among several people. The accompanying side dishes are also neatly seasoned, making for a satisfying and filling meal.

[기본 제공]

• 헬멧, 장갑, 휴대폰 거치대, 라이딩자켓(무료 대여가능)

• 필요 시 추천 라이딩 코스 안내 가능

• 짐 보관 서비스 제공

• 음료 서비스 제공

[이용 대상]

• 유효한 모터사이클 운전면허를 소지한 국내·외 이용객

• 국제운전면허증 또는 한국에서 인정되는 면허 소지 외국인 이용 가능

[기타 사항]

• 외국인 자차·자손 보험 가입 가능

第二届AECHAE林再次将自然与艺术汇聚一堂。

饱含自然细腻意趣的盆景、尽显各类素材独特魅力的工艺作品，以及触动人心的绘画作品，将在AECHAE的空间之中，各自讲述独属于自己的故事。


如同各式各样的自然要素汇聚在一起构筑成生态系统一般，不同领域的艺术门类彼此协作、交融共鸣，共同造就一片丰盈绚烂的“森林”。
